newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen top-heavy, focus on mark/yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen top-heavy, focus on mark/yen.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be top-heavy during Asian trading time on Friday with possible exporter sales above 113.20 yen, but bids from Japanese investors are likely to kick in on downside to support the dollar, dealers said.

The market will focus on moves in mark/yen after the mark pared recent losses against major currencies overnight following comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, who said the dollar's recovery against the mark from historic lows in 1995 was complete. Dealers said Tokyo traders are likely to cover their mark short positions during Asian time.
Overnight, the dollar fell more than two pfennigs from the high of 1.7664 marks set in Tokyo, where dealers extended this week's string of powerful gains to another peak not seen since February 1994.

Traders started to buy back marks after Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said the central bank was watching foreign exchange developments closely and believed the dollar/mark was now "in a phase in which the (post-1995) correction has clearly come to an end".
He also said that it is important that the mark remains a strong currency and enters the euro as a strong currency.
"With Tietmeyer's comments, traders may start a downside probe in dollar/mark trade," the city bank dealer said.

In overseas trade on Thursday, an expected quarter-point rise in Britain's official interest rates led to a wave of sterling/mark sales from traders who had been anticipating a more aggressive half-point rise in rates. This also put pressure on the dollar/mark rate.
